back: A pronounced bend in a river: river cliff (outside, erosion) and slip-off slope (inside, deposition).
Outer-bank erosion narrows the neck → flood cuts through → new straight channel → deposition seals the old bend.
Wide flat land beside a lower-course river, built of alluvium deposited in floods.
Natural raised bank beside the channel, built of coarse material dropped first in floods.
Deposits at a river mouth where sediment supply exceeds removal by waves and currents; crossed by distributaries.
Arcuate (fan, e.g. Nile); bird's-foot (long fingers, e.g. Mississippi); estuarine (fills an estuary).
Channel split by bars of sediment into many interlinking channels; large load and variable discharge.
Zambezi floodplain below the escarpment; named after four pools left as old river channels; part of a World Heritage Site.
Channel length ÷ straight-line distance. About 1 = straight; above about 1.5 = meandering.
